<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Simple linear regression with a binary predictor</h1>
  <p>When a predictor has exactly two groups, <code>lm()</code> draws a line between two group means. You will fit models, read coefficients as differences, and see how changing the reference level relabels (but does not change) the underlying relationship.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

A <strong>binary predictor</strong> takes only two values, such as female vs male or smoker vs nonsmoker. In R you still write a familiar formula:

```r
lm(outcome ~ group, data = my_data)
```

R turns the group into a <strong>dummy variable</strong>: 0 for the <strong>reference</strong> level and 1 for the other level. The intercept is the mean of the reference group; the slope is the <strong>difference in means</strong> between the two groups.

This practical uses teaching datasets from common R packages:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><code>openintro::births14</code>: US live births (birth weight by sex)</li>
  <li><code>MASS::birthwt</code>: Baystate birth weights (birth weight by smoking status)</li>
  <li><code>DAAG::ais</code>: Australian Institute of Sport athletes (serum ferritin by sex)</li>
</ul>

After answering the questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>In a regression with a binary predictor, the intercept $b_0$ equals:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">The overall mean of the outcome, pooling both groups.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">The mean of the outcome in the <strong>reference</strong> group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="c">The difference in means between the two groups.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. When every dummy is 0, you are in the reference group, so the intercept is that group's mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. The intercept is the predicted outcome when the dummy equals 0, which is the reference group's mean."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>The slope $b_1$ for the non-reference level tells you:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">How much higher (or lower) the other group's mean is compared with the reference group.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">The mean of the non-reference group on its own.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="c">Whether the relationship is linear.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The slope is a difference in means, not a standalone mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. The slope is the gap between group means. To get the other group's mean, add the slope to the intercept."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The equation</h2>

<div class="formula-panel">

$$\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 \cdot x$$

<p><strong>Reading the pieces for a binary predictor:</strong></p>
<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>$x = 0$ for the reference group; $x = 1$ for the other group.</li>
  <li>$b_0$ = mean of $y$ in the reference group.</li>
  <li>$b_1$ = difference in means (other group minus reference group).</li>
</ul>

</div>

```{=html}
<div class="svg-panel" aria-label="Two group means connected by a regression line">
<svg viewBox="0 0 760 260" role="img">
  <rect width="760" height="260" rx="8" fill="#fff"/>
  <line x1="70" y1="30" x2="70" y2="210" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.4"/>
  <line x1="70" y1="210" x2="700" y2="210" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.4"/>
  <text x="24" y="125" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#5d7475" transform="rotate(-90,24,125)">Outcome (y)</text>
  <line x1="220" y1="130" x2="560" y2="95" stroke="#00565e" stroke-width="3"/>
  <circle cx="220" cy="130" r="7" fill="#2f5f98" stroke="#1d4275" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <circle cx="560" cy="95" r="7" fill="#00565e" stroke="#003f45" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <line x1="220" y1="130" x2="560" y2="130" stroke="#b83b5e" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="5,3"/>
  <line x1="560" y1="130" x2="560" y2="95" stroke="#b83b5e" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <text x="220" y="118" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="800" fill="#2f5f98">b₀ = ref. mean</text>
  <text x="575" y="118" font-size="11" font-weight="800" fill="#b83b5e">b₁ = difference</text>
  <text x="220" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#173234">Reference (x = 0)</text>
  <text x="560" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#173234">Other group (x = 1)</text>
</svg>
<p class="svg-caption">With a binary predictor, the fitted line is just the segment joining the two group means.</p>
</div>
```

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 1: birth weight by sex (<code>openintro::births14</code>)</h2>

The <code>births14</code> dataset is a random sample of US live births in 2014. We will model birth weight in pounds (<code>weight</code>) from the baby's sex (<code>sex</code>: female or male).

First, load the data and set <strong>female</strong> as the reference level. Then fit the model and inspect the output.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: births14, female reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(openintro)
library(dplyr)
data(births14)

births14 <- births14 |>
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")))

mod_sex <- lm(weight ~ sex, data = births14)
summary(mod_sex)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>With <strong>female</strong> as the reference level, what is the predicted birth weight for a <strong>female</strong> baby (in pounds, to two decimal places)?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">7.02</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">0.36</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="c">7.38</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The intercept (about 7.02 lb) is the female mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. Look at the (Intercept) row. That is the female mean because female is the reference level."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>What is the predicted birth weight for a <strong>male</strong> baby?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">7.02 lb</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">0.36 lb</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="c">7.38 lb (about 7.02 + 0.36)</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Add the sexmale slope to the intercept: about 7.02 + 0.36 ≈ 7.38 lb." data-incorrect="Not quite. Male mean = intercept + sexmale coefficient ≈ 7.02 + 0.36."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 5</div>
  <p>The coefficient on <code>sexmale</code> is about +0.36. In plain language, this means male babies weigh on average:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="a">0.36 lb in total.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b">About 0.36 lb <strong>more</strong> than female babies.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="c">About 0.36 lb less than female babies.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The slope is a difference vs the reference group, not a standalone mean." data-incorrect="Not quite. A positive slope means the non-reference group is higher than the reference group by that amount."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Switching the reference level</h2>

The reference level is a <strong>labeling choice</strong>. The gap between group means stays the same; only the intercept and the sign of the slope change.

Re-run the model below with <strong>male</strong> as the reference. Compare the output to the previous cell.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: relevel sex to male reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
births14_m <- births14 |>
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, levels = c("male", "female")))

mod_sex_male_ref <- lm(weight ~ sex, data = births14_m)
summary(mod_sex_male_ref)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 6</div>
  <p>When male is the reference level, the coefficient on <code>sexfemale</code> is about −0.36. Why is it negative?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="a">Female babies weigh less than male babies, and female is now compared with male as reference.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="b">The relationship reversed; males now weigh less than females.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="c">R made a mistake when releveling.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The underlying means are unchanged; the sign flips because the reference group flipped." data-incorrect="Not quite. Releveling changes labels, not the data. Females are still lighter on average; the slope now measures female minus male."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 7</div>
  <p>Comparing the two models (female reference vs male reference), the <strong>magnitude</strong> of the sex difference is:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="a">Larger when male is reference.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="b">The same (about 0.36 lb).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="c">Impossible to compare.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. |+0.36| = |−0.36|; only the sign and intercept changed." data-incorrect="Not quite. The absolute difference in group means is unchanged."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Worked example 2: birth weight by smoking (<code>MASS::birthwt</code>)</h2>

The classic <code>birthwt</code> data record birth weight in grams (<code>bwt</code>) and whether the mother smoked during pregnancy (<code>smoke</code>: 0 = no, 1 = yes). We treat nonsmokers as the reference group.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: birthwt, nonsmoker reference</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
data(birthwt)

birthwt <- birthwt |>
  mutate(smoke = factor(smoke, levels = c(0, 1),
                        labels = c("nonsmoker", "smoker")))

mod_smoke <- lm(bwt ~ smoke, data = birthwt)
summary(mod_smoke)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 8</div>
  <p>The intercept is about 3056 g. Whose mean birth weight does that represent?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="a">Babies whose mothers did <strong>not</strong> smoke during pregnancy.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="b">Babies whose mothers smoked during pregnancy.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="c">All babies in the dataset combined.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Nonsmoker is the reference level (smoke = 0)." data-incorrect="Not quite. The intercept is always the reference group mean. Here nonsmoker is reference."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 9</div>
  <p>The <code>smokesmoker</code> coefficient is about −284 g. The predicted mean birth weight for smokers is approximately:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="a">284 g</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="b">2772 g (3056 − 284)</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="c">3340 g (3056 + 284)</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Smoker mean = intercept + slope ≈ 3056 − 284 ≈ 2772 g." data-incorrect="Not quite. Add the smoker coefficient to the intercept. The negative slope means smokers are lower."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 10</div>
  <p>Suppose you relevel so <strong>smoker</strong> is the reference in <code>birthwt</code>. The coefficient for <code>nonsmoker</code> would be about:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="a">−284 g</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="b">+284 g</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="c">3056 g</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Nonsmokers weigh about 284 g more than smokers; the sign flips when smoker becomes reference." data-incorrect="Not quite. When smoker is reference, nonsmoker is above smoker by about 284 g, so the coefficient is positive."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 1: fill in the model formula (<code>DAAG::ais</code>)</h2>

The <code>ais</code> dataset contains physiological measurements on elite athletes. Fit a model predicting serum ferritin (<code>ferr</code>, ng/mL) from sex (<code>sex</code>: <code>f</code> or <code>m</code>).

Replace each `____` with the correct variable name, then run the cell.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: exercise 1 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(DAAG)
data(ais)

mod_ferr <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = ais)
summary(mod_ferr)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
mod_ferr <- lm(ferr ~ sex, data = ais)
```

The intercept (about 57) is the mean ferritin for females (<code>f</code> is the default reference). The <code>sexm</code> row (about +39) says males average about 39 ng/mL higher.

</details>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Exercise 2: relevel and refit (<code>births14</code>)</h2>

Complete the code below to set <strong>female</strong> as the reference level for <code>sex</code>, then fit <code>weight ~ sex</code>. Replace each `____`.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: exercise 2 (fill in blanks)</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(openintro)
library(dplyr)
data(births14)

births14 <- births14 |>
  mutate(sex = factor(____, levels = c("____", "male")))

mod_fill <- lm(____ ~ ____, data = births14)
summary(mod_fill)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
births14 <- births14 |>
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")))

mod_fill <- lm(weight ~ sex, data = births14)
```

</details>

</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "BINREF25";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 10;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
